courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: 3D Printing for Engineering Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Laboratory 3 hours, Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of rapid technologies in Additive Manufacturing that are high productivity tools designed to cut lead times, reduce time to market, increase the quality of the product, and improve collaboration within the organization.

courses.title: Mechanics I - Statics for Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches Newton's laws, resultants and equilibrium of force systems, trusses and frames, determination of centroids, and distributed loads and moments of inertia. Introduces dry friction and force systems in space.

courses.title: Mechanisms
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the purpose and actions of cams, gear trains, levers, and other mechanical devices used to transmit control. Focuses on motions, linkages, velocities, and acceleration of points within a link mechanism; layout method for designing cams and gear grain. Requires preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Basic Fluid Mechanics - Hydraulics/Pneumatics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces theory, operation and maintenance of hydraulic/ pneumatics devices and systems. Emphasizes the properties of fluids, fluid flow, fluid statics, and the application of Bernoulli's equation.

courses.title: Machine Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the design of machine elements for producing and transmitting power. Includes additional material in statics, strength of materials, dynamics, engineering materials and industrial processes, including lubrication and friction. Emphasizes graphical kinematics of mechanisms, and discusses analytical design of machine components. Requires preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Machine Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces analytical design of bearings, clutches, coupling, brakes, springs, gearing systems, and power shafting. Emphasizes methods of construction, machine parts and specifications of materials, and manufacturing processes. Part II of II.

courses.title: Mental Health Skill Training I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills necessary to function as a mental health worker, with emphasis on guided practice in counseling skills as well as improved self-awareness. Includes training in problem-solving, goal-setting, and implementation of appropriate strategies and evaluation techniques relating to interaction involving a variety of client needs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Mental Health Skill Training II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills necessary to function as a mental health worker, with emphasis on guided practice in counseling skills as well as improved self-awareness. Includes training in problem-solving, goal-setting, and implementation of appropriate strategies and evaluation techniques relating to interaction involving a variety of client needs. Part II of II.

courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles, methods, and problems involved in marketing to consumers and organizational buyers. Discusses problems and policies connected with distribution and sale of products, pricing, promotion, and buyer motivation. Examines variations of marketing research, legal, social, ethical, e-commerce, and international considerations in marketing.

courses.title: Principles of Selling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a fundamental, skills-based approach to selling and relationship building. Emphasizes learning effective interpersonal communication skills in all areas of the sales process through skill-building activities. Examines entry-level sales careers in retailing, wholesaling, services and industrial selling.

courses.title: Customer Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the concepts of marketing as they relate to customer service. Teaches development of customer service training and implementation of strategies to improve customer relations and service. Includes lecture, role-playing, and case studies.

courses.title: Introduction to Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the discipline of marketing and the need to create customer value and relationships in the marketplace. Presents an overview of the marketing principles and management strategies, along with the analytical tools used by organizations in the creation of a marketing plan.

courses.title: Sales and Marketing Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the relationship of professional sales skills and marketing management techniques. Demonstrates the use of the Internet to enhance marketing. Studies legal and ethical considerations.

courses.title: Retail Organization and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the organization of the retail establishment to accomplish its goals in an effective and efficient manner. Includes study of site location, internal layout, store operations, and security. Examines the retailing mix, the buying or procurement process, pricing, and selling. Studies retail advertising, promotion, and publicity as a coordinated effort to increase store traffic.

courses.title: Public Relations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces public relations as a marketing activity and focuses on media relations, publicity, strategic planning, public relations research, communication with multiple audiences, and the elements of an effective public relations campaign to influence public opinion. Equips students with the basic skills for writing publicity materials and coordinating public relations campaigns and media kits. This course applies basic writing and communication skills to the principles of public relations. This is an upper level course intended for students planning to study in public relations or a related field. This course is cross-listed with CST 221 . Credit will not be awarded for both.

courses.title: Customer Service Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the role of customer service in achieving a firm's long-term goals; discuses the basic principles of effective customer service; explores the tasks and responsibilities of a customer service manager. Includes such topics as purpose of customer service; establishment of customer service goals and policies; recruitment, selection and training of customer service employees motivation techniques; empowering employees for better decision making; and evaluation of customer service employees and program.

courses.title: Social Media Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Credit Hours: 3, Lecture Hours: 3, Lab Hours: 0, Total Contact Hours: 3
courses.description: Surveys the use of social networks and online communities such as blogs, wikis, virtual events that allow companies to expand their interaction with customers and develop relationships with collaborative communities. Emphasizes the ongoing transformation of the way companies adjust their marketing plans to improve interaction with customers online.

courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Admission to AFROTC program. Co-requisite: Leadership Laboratory.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the United States Air Force and Air Force Reserve Officers' Training Corps. Includes the mission and organization of the Air Force, officership and professionalism, military customs and courtesies, Air Force officer opportunities, and an introduction to communication skills. [PVCC Students will take AIRS classes at the University of Virginia for PVCC credit.] Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Army ROTC
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the first year of general military science: organization of the army and ROTC, U.S. Army and national security, individual weapons, marksmanship, and leadership laboratory. Courses offered only in cooperation with four- year colleges authorized to offer Army ROTC programs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Leadership
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the first year of general military science: organization of the army and ROTC, U.S. Army and national security, individual weapons, marksmanship, and leadership laboratory. Courses offered only in cooperation with four- year colleges authorized to offer Army ROTC programs. Part II of II.

courses.title: The Evolution of Air and Space Power
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Admission to AFROTC program. Co-requisite: Leadership Laboratory.
courses.description: Examines general aspects of air and space power through a historical perspective. Covers a time period from the first balloons and dirigibles to the use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles in today's technologically advanced Air Force. Historical examples serve to extrapolate the development of Air Force capabilities (competencies) and missions (functions) to demonstrate the evolution of what has become today's USAF air and space power. Examines several fundamental truths associated with war in the third dimension; e.g. Principles of War and Tenets of Air and Space Power. Provides a knowledge-level understanding for the general element and employment of air and space power from an institutional, doctrinal, and historical perspective. Continues a discussion of the importance of the Air Force Core Values through use of operational examples and historical Air Force leaders and develops cadets' communication skills. Part I of II.

courses.description: Focuses on the second year of general military science: American military history, introduction to operations and basic tactics, map and aerial photo reading, and leadership laboratory.
